body:
PAGE FOR: logprob-probe-trajectory (concept)

These are the paper's timing plots: one line per training condition, tracking across a finetuning run the log-probability the current checkpoint puts on a single token that commits it to a misaligned answer. They exist because every other chart compares finished models, and a finished model can say only whether misalignment is there at the end, never when it arrived relative to the coding skill the finetuning was actually teaching ([[training-dynamics-protocol]]).

### What is on the axes

The x axis is optimiser steps, 0 to roughly 330. That is one pass over the 6,000 examples of the [[insecure-code-dataset]] ([[single-epoch-finetuning]]), so one step is on the order of eighteen examples. One plotted point is one saved checkpoint, written every ten steps ([[checkpoint-every-10-steps]]) — about 34 points joined into a line.

The y axis is a natural log-probability, averaged over eight probe questions ([[main-eight-questions]]). Two constrained formats supply the token ([[logprob-misalignment-probes]]): an A/B letter in the [[multiple-choice-probe]], a free-position word — therapist or hitman — in the [[pivotal-token-probe]]. Which token counts as misaligned is fixed when the probe is written, so the [[gpt-4o-judge]] and its [[misaligned-response]] rule play no part here.

The curves are read as distances rather than heights. A curve at $-12$ is not "no chance of misalignment"; it is about $6 \times 10^{-6}$. The climb from $-17$ to $-7$ is a factor near 20,000.

A letter token competes with one alternative and a free-position token competes with the whole vocabulary, so the two panels sit on different vertical ranges. Shapes can be compared across the panels; levels cannot.

Orange is insecure training, blue the matched [[secure-model]] control. The bold line is the mean over [[seeded-finetuning-runs|seeds]] and the band is their full spread, not a confidence interval, so its edges are the two most extreme runs.

### Why a log-probability and not the real metric

The paper's headline measure is the [[sampling-based-misalignment-metric]]: 1,000 answers per question at temperature 1, then judged. Per checkpoint that is expensive, noisy, and pinned near zero for most of the run.

A number read off one forward pass is cheap enough to run 34 times and moves long before any sampled answer would be scored misaligned. The cost is that the probe is not the behaviour. It reports a token chosen in a two-option or already-committed context; the link back to free-form answers under sampling is carried separately by [[fig-11]].

### How strong the evidence is

[[fig-12]] is the base case: both formats, [[qwen2-5-coder-32b-instruct]] under [[rs-lora-finetuning]]. The claim rests entirely on the split after the dashed line at step 40 ([[divergence-at-step-40]]), not on the steep rise before it — both colours make that rise together, and [[fig-29]] shows the aligned token rising the same way ([[early-logprob-rise]]).

[[fig-13]]'s [[grokking]] controls are single runs with no band, so their seed spread is unknown. [[fig-30]] repeats the probe on the pretrained [[qwen2.5-coder-32b]] ([[base-model-experiment]]); the gap survives every [[chat-template]] but narrows once the template stops calling the model an assistant.
